sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 早上好，各位。

sentences.en: I've been invited to talk about my research project into Australian Aboriginal rock paintings.
sentences.zh: 我受邀来谈谈我对澳大利亚原住民岩画的研究项目。

sentences.en: The Australian Aborigines have recorded both real and symbolic images of their time on rock walls for many thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚原住民数千年以来，一直在岩壁上记录他们时代的真实与象征性图像。

sentences.en: Throughout the long history of this tradition, new images have appeared and new painting styles have developed.
sentences.zh: 在这一传统漫长的历史进程中，新的图像不断出现，新的绘画风格也逐渐发展起来。

sentences.en: And these characteristics can be used to categorise the different artistic styles.
sentences.zh: 这些特征可用于对不同艺术风格进行分类。

sentences.en: Among these are what we call the Dynamic, Yam and Modern styles of painting.
sentences.zh: 其中就包括我们所称的‘动态式’、‘山药式’和‘现代式’绘画风格。

sentences.en: One of the most significant characteristics of the different styles is the way that humans are depicted in the paintings.
sentences.zh: 不同风格最显著的特征之一，是画中人物形象的表现方式。

sentences.en: The more recent paintings show people in static poses.
sentences.zh: 较近期的绘画中，人物呈现静止的姿态。

sentences.en: But the first human images to dominate rock art paintings, over 8,000 years ago, were full of movement.
sentences.zh: 但早在八千多年前，最早占据岩画主导地位的人物形象则充满动感。

sentences.en: These paintings showed people hunting and cooking food and so they were given the name 'Dynamic' to reflect this energy.
sentences.zh: 这些绘画描绘了人们狩猎和烹煮食物的场景，因此被命名为‘动态式’，以体现这种活力。

sentences.en: It's quite amazing considering they were painted in such a simple stick-like form.
sentences.zh: 考虑到它们是以极为简朴的棍状形式绘制而成，这的确令人惊叹。

sentences.en: In the Yam period, a there was a movement away from stick figures to a more naturalistic shape.
sentences.zh: 在‘山药时期’，绘画风格开始从棍状人形转向更为写实的形态。

sentences.en: However, they didn't go as far as the Modern style, which is known as 'x-ray' because it actually makes a feature of the internal skeleton as well as the organs of animals and humans.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种风格尚未达到‘现代式’的程度；‘现代式’又称‘X光式’，因其不仅描绘动物和人类的外部轮廓，还特意刻画其内部骨骼及器官。

sentences.en: The Yam style of painting got its name from the fact that it featured much curvier figures that actually resemble the vegetable called a yam, which a is similar to a sweet potato.
sentences.zh: ‘山药式’绘画得名于其人物形象曲线更为明显，酷似一种名为‘山药’的蔬菜（类似于甘薯）。

sentences.en: The Modern paintings are interesting because they include paintings at the time of the first contact with European settlers.
sentences.zh: ‘现代式’绘画颇为有趣，因为其中包含了欧洲殖民者首次抵达时的相关画面。

sentences.en: Aborigines managed to convey the idea of the settlers' clothing by simply painting the Europeans without any hands, indicating the habit of standing with their hands in their pockets!
sentences.zh: 原住民仅通过将欧洲人画成没有双手的形象，便巧妙传达出殖民者着装的特点——暗示他们习惯将双手插在口袋里！

sentences.en: Size is another characteristic.
sentences.zh: 尺寸是另一项特征。

sentences.en: The more recent images tend to be life size or even larger, but the Dynamic figures are painted in miniature.
sentences.zh: 较近期的图像往往接近真人大小甚至更大，而‘动态式’人物则以微型尺寸绘制。

sentences.en: Aboriginal rock art also records the environmental changes that occurred over thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚原住民岩画还记录了数千年来发生的环境变迁。

sentences.en: For example, we know from the Dynamic paintings that over 8,000 years ago, Aborigines would have rarely eaten fish and sea levels were much lower at this time.
sentences.zh: 例如，从‘动态式’绘画中我们得知，八千多年前，原住民极少食用鱼类，且当时海平面远低于现今水平。

sentences.en: In fact, fish didn't start to appear in paintings until the Yam period along with shells and other marine images.
sentences.zh: 事实上，鱼类直到‘山药时期’才开始出现在绘画中，同时出现的还有贝壳及其他海洋生物图像。

sentences.en: The paintings of the Yam tradition also suggest that, during this time, the Aborigines moved away from animals as their main food source and began including vegetables in their diet, as these feature prominently.
sentences.zh: ‘山药式’绘画传统还表明，在此期间，原住民逐渐减少以动物为主要食物来源，转而将蔬菜纳入日常饮食，因为蔬菜形象在画中十分突出。

sentences.en: Freshwater creatures didn't appear in the paintings until the Modern period from 4,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 淡水生物直到距今四千年的‘现代时期’才出现在绘画中。

sentences.en: So, these paintings have already taught us a lot.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些绘画已为我们提供了大量信息。

sentences.en: But one image that has always intrigued us is known as the 'Rainbow Serpent'.
sentences.zh: 但有一幅始终令我们着迷的图像被称为‘彩虹蛇’。

sentences.en: The Rainbow Serpent, which is the focus of my www.TopSage.com 7. 5500 most recent project, gets its name from its snake or serpent-like body and it first appeared Sage.com in the Yam period 4 to 6,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: ‘彩虹蛇’——即我最近研究项目的核心主题——得名于其蛇或蟒蛇般的身体形态，最早出现于距今四千至六千年前的‘山药时期’。

sentences.en: Many believe it is a curious mixture of kangaroo,- snake and crocodile.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为它是一种袋鼠、蛇与鳄鱼的奇特混合体。

sentences.en: But we decided to study the Rainbow Serpent paintings to see if we could locate the animal that the very first painters based their image on.
sentences.zh: 但我们决定专门研究‘彩虹蛇’的绘画作品，以确定最早绘制该形象的画家究竟以何种动物为原型。

sentences.en: The Yam period coincided with the end of the last ice age.
sentences.zh: ‘山药时期’恰逢上一个冰河时代的末期。

sentences.en: This brought about tremendous change in the environment, with the sea levels rising and creeping steadily inland.
sentences.zh: 这引发了环境的巨大变化：海平面持续上升并不断向内陆推进。

sentences.en: This flooded many familiar land features and also caused a great deal of disruption to traditional patterns of life, hunting in particular.
sentences.zh: 许多人们熟悉的陆地地貌因此被淹没，传统生活方式——尤其是狩猎模式——也受到严重干扰。

sentences.en: New shores were formed and totally different creatures would have washed up onto the shores.
sentences.zh: 新的海岸线形成，各种截然不同的生物随之被冲上岸。

sentences.en: We studied 107 paintings of the Rainbow Serpent and found that the one creature that matches it most closely was the Ribboned Pipefish, which is a type of sea horse.
sentences.zh: 我们研究了107幅‘彩虹蛇’绘画，发现与其形态最为吻合的生物是带状管海马（一种海马）。

sentences.en: This sea creature would a have been a totally unfamiliar sight in the inland regions where the image is found and may have been the inspiration behind the early paintings.
sentences.zh: 这种海洋生物对于‘彩虹蛇’图像所在内陆地区而言，完全是一种前所未见的景象，或许正是早期绘画创作的灵感来源。

sentences.en: So, at the end of the ice age there would have been enormous changes in animal and plant life.
sentences.zh: 因此，冰河时代结束之际，动植物界均发生了巨大变化。

sentences.en: It's not surprising then, that the Aborigines linked this abundance to the new creatures they witnessed.
sentences.zh: 原住民将这种生机勃发的景象与他们目睹的新生物联系起来，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Even today, Aborigines see the Rainbow Serpent as a symbol of creation, which is understandable given the increase in vegetation and the new life forms that featured when the image first appeared.
sentences.zh: 直至今日，原住民仍将‘彩虹蛇’视为创世的象征；鉴于图像初现之时植被繁茂、新生命形式涌现，这种理解完全可以理解。
